title: HSMU-SpGEMM: Achieving High Shared Memory Utilization for Parallel Sparse General Matrix-Matrix Multiplication on Modern GPUs
problem: Hash-based SpGEMM algorithms on GPUs fail to simultaneously minimize hash collisions and efficiently utilize fast shared memory, causing significant performance degradation when executing sparse general matrix-matrix multiplication.
motivation: SpGEMM is a core primitive for scientific computing, and the memory bandwidth and shared memory capacity of modern GPUs are underutilized by existing hash-based approaches, leaving substantial performance on the table.
method: HSMU-SpGEMM introduces a novel accumulator design that maximizes shared memory utilization on modern GPUs by rethinking the hash-based accumulation strategy to reduce collision overhead while packing more active data into shared memory. The approach also optimizes the symbolic stages of SpGEMM (row count, product computation) to complement the new accumulator. Evaluation is performed on three GPU microarchitectures (Ampere, Ada Lovelace, Turing).
key_novelty: A new GPU accumulator design that achieves high shared memory utilization for SpGEMM by decoupling collision reduction from memory packing efficiency.
contributions: Novel accumulator design achieving high shared memory utilization for SpGEMM on modern GPUs
Optimization of symbolic SpGEMM stages to complement the new accumulator
Significant performance improvements over four state-of-the-art hash-based SpGEMM libraries (Nsparse, spECK, OpSparse, cuSPARSE) across three GPU generations

metrics.speedup: significant improvement over Nsparse, spECK, OpSparse, cuSPARSE (exact numbers not stated in abstract)
